main_body: Timber-framed house with a large red tile roof (hip roof with a front gable) over plaster-and-beam walls, a door and a window, plus a lower gabled porch at the front
top_band: At x=107, tile roof slopes in orange, red and plum tiles, rows 4-43 under the outline at rows 2-3. Rows 44-45 are a dark eave line, then the front face starts: grey gutter ledge rows 46-48, then wall from row 49.
evidence: The roof is drawn as large sloped top surfaces: hip planes with per-tile highlights and a ridge row of bright tiles. The south walls sit below it, separated by a dark eave line and a grey ledge. The wall has timber beams, a recessed window with a sill and an inset door. The lower porch repeats the same structure with its own gable roof above its wall. There is no isometric side face, and every major part shows both a top surface and a front face.

style.evidence: The candidate has 202 distinct colours and a median of 18 colours per tile, equal to house-h101_0 and above house-h112_0-stone. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Only 12% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines are tinted: dark brown beside timber and dark plum-red beside tiles. The roof tiles have per-tile highlights and several tone steps. The plaster has speckle and the timbers have grain. It would sit next to the references without looking thinner.
